{{Quote|This is Eris Herro ''[sic]'' of ENS, embedded with the 77th Air Wing at Kelrodo-Ai.|Eris Harro|<ref name="TGOKA" />}}
'''Eris Harro''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]]<ref name="TGOKA" /> individual from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], who was an heiress of one of the world's [[Quintad/Legends|Quintad]] houses.<ref name="TEGTW" /> During the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Harro worked as reporter for the [[Eriadu News Service]]. and in [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]], she traveled to the war-torn planet [[Kelrodo-Ai/Legends|Kelrodo-Ai]] along with an ENS news team, to interview the Imperial [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Shea Hublin]] of the [[77th Air Wing]]. Hublin was leading a [[Battle of Kelrodo-Ai|campaign]] to rid the world of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|holdout forces]] as part of the Empire's wider [[Western Reaches Operation]], and he spoke to Harro about the battle. Once she had concluded her interview Hublin, Harro and the rest of the news team quickly departed from the planet.<ref name="TGOKA" />

Following the conclusion of the Western Reaches Operation, Hublin was granted a marquisate on Eriadu, and he and Harro became married. In [[13 BBY/Legends|13 BBY]], Hublin lost his [[Limb/Legends|leg]] and half of his right arm during a battle, which led Harro to demand that he retire from the [[Starfighter Corps/Legends|Starfighter Corps]].<ref name="TEGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
Eris Harro was created by the writer [[Jason Fry]] and she first appeared in [[The Guns of Kelrodo-Ai (short story)|''The Guns of Kelrodo-Ai'']], a short story that was published in the magazine [[Star Wars Insider 132|''Star Wars Insider'' 132]] in [[2012]]. ''The Guns of Kelrodo-Ai'' was intended to act as a tie-in to the reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' and Harro subsequently received a mention in the reference book itself. However, there is a discrepancy between the two sources regarding the spelling of her name; ''The Guns of Kelrodo-Ai'' refers to her as "Eris Herro," while ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' spells her name "Eris Harro." This article uses the spelling given in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', because the the guide book was the most recently-released of the two sources.
